primary_claim: A sparse autoencoder trained on Whisper-Tiny's last encoder-layer activations goes from 0% to 48% sparsity and surfaces features correlated with speaker accent, but does not yield features that separate gender (essentially zero recall for the female class with a Random Forest predictor).
stated_future_work: Explore the decoder in addition to the encoder, focused on the relationship between encoder embeddings and transcription
Train more SAEs on other encoder and decoder layers, not just the single layer explored
Explore more demographics and feature ideas beyond gender and accent
limitations_stated: Author took on more than their mechinterp knowledge could fully support for this project
Gender labels limited to male/female/other per CommonVoice metadata, limiting inclusiveness of analysis
Could not build an accent predictor analogous to the gender one due to small dataset size
384-dimensional non-sparse residual stream activations are difficult to interpret directly, motivating the SAE approach
quote: we go from 0 sparsity in the original space to 48% sparse in the encoded space of the SAE.
